newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Qantas service jobs to be tendered-union.
newsitem.headline: Qantas service jobs to be tendered-union.

text.p: Qantas Airways Ltd will seek tenders for customer service and ramp services work at Brisbane, Melbourne and Perth airports, union officials said on Monday.
Members of the Australian Services Union (ASU) working for Qantas will hold meetings later on Monday to consider their options, the union said in a statement.
Qantas officials were not available for comment.
"Qantas has announced its intention to seek tenders for customer service and ramp services work at Brisbane, Melbourne and Perth airports," the statement said.
"The union understands that virtually everyone who works on the ground for Qantas at these airports will have their positions subject to tender," it said.
"Qantas expects its own staff to be part of the tender process by forming internal bid teams. Estimates of the worth of these contracts are in the many millions of dollars."

The ASU is one of Australia's largest unions with about 180,000 members across Australia, covers a wide range of white collar employees at airports from the check-in counter to load control and movement control.
"This announcement by Qantas threatens our member's jobs as they will be forced to bid for their jobs against some very large multinationals," ASU National Secretary Paul Slape said.
"Our members say this process is only designed to drive wages and conditions down and force redundancies."

The ASU said it estimated that about 1,000 of its members in Brisbane, Perth and Melbourne will be effected by this move. "It is likely that the jobs of many members of the Transport Workers Unions will also be involved," it said.
Qantas is 25 percent owned by British Airways Plc
